newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl's CDU unscathed by euro, gold debate - poll.
newsitem.headline: Kohl's CDU unscathed by euro, gold debate - poll.

text.p: A poll released on Monday showed Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) were relstively unscathed by debate over German entry into European monetary union (EMU) and a row over Bundesbank gold reserves.

A survey done by the Bonn-based Infas institute and published by the Frankfurter Allgemeine newspaper showed the CDU and its Christian Social Union (CSU) Bavarian sister party could even be profiting from the political turbulence.

The survey of 1,007 people on June 2-4 followed an unprecedented dispute between the government and the Bundesbank over Bonn's plan to revalue central bank assets to help it qualify for the 1999 launch of Europe's planned single currency, the euro.

Four of 10 respondents agreed with the statement, "The Union (of CDU and CSU) is drawing the greatest benefit from the discussion over the euro", while only 20 percent believed the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) were benefiting.
No smaller party, including the CDU/CSU's junior coalition partner the Free Democrats (FDP) on whom Kohl relies for his parliamentary majority, was perceived as coming out of the debate favourably.
Infas did not say why respondents felt the government parties were undamaged or even strengthened from the gold reserves affair.
Kohl's government later backed down on the plan to revalue gold and currency reserves in the face of Bundesbank opposition.
